brief:
Build the Lumen DESIGN SYSTEM that every scene, mini-game and engagement system will use. Keep every existing export of src/ui-kit/context.tsx working (ServicesProvider, useServices, useSignal, useRegistry, asComponent, HudSlot) — you may add to it.

1) CSS: tokens.css + base.css imported from src/ui-kit/index.ts. Tokens as CSS custom properties: palette from GAME_DESIGN.md §3 (ink/aubergine backgrounds, candle gold, ivory text, muted, system accents, clinical normal/abnormal/critical), typography (Fraunces Variable display, Inter Variable UI, Space Grotesk numbers — fonts are already loaded by the app), type scale, spacing scale, radii, layered shadows & glows, glass surface recipe (backdrop-filter, luminous 1px borders, inner highlight), easing curves (out-expo, spring overshoot), durations, z-index layers. html.high-contrast and html.reduced-motion variants + prefers-reduced-motion. base.css: reset, body background, custom scrollbars, gorgeous focus-visible rings, ::selection, utility classes kept minimal.

2) Components (Preact, typed props, accessible, each with hover/press/focus states and micro-animations): Button (variants: primary-gold, glass, ghost, danger; sizes; leading icon; loading; satisfying press), IconButton, GlassPanel/Card (optional accent glow, header slot), Modal/Dialog (portal-less overlay, focus trap, Esc, animated scale+blur in), Tabs, Chip, Badge, ProgressBar & RingMeter (animated fill), CountUp (animated number, Space Grotesk), Stars (0-3 with fill animation), GradeStamp (S/A/B/C/D/F — dramatic rubber-stamp slam animation, S is iridescent gold), Tooltip, ToastHost (listens to services.bus 'toast' events, stacks, auto-dismiss, tone colours), RewardChip (renders a RewardGrant with rarity glow: common/rare/epic/legendary), SpeechBubble with typewriter text reveal (skippable on click), Ornament/Divider (gold filigree SVG), Kbd, ScrollArea, Screen layout (fixed full-viewport scene frame with top bar: left/right HudSlot areas + title + back button), and Backdrop: an animated scene background (night gradient, slow drifting light motes/bokeh on a canvas, optional rain-on-glass streaks, film grain overlay, vignette) with variants 'title' | 'hub' | 'exam' | 'emergency' | 'results' | 'calm'; must be cheap (pause when hidden, DPR-aware, reduced-motion = static).

3) Icon: an <Icon name=... /> component with a cohesive hand-tuned SVG line-icon set (1.75px strokes, rounded) covering: each TestId in core/tests.ts (visual-acuity chart, pinhole, retinoscope, phoropter, keratometer, penlight/pupils, occluder/cover-test, motility H, convergence, colour plate, amsler grid, visual field, slit lamp, fluorescein drop, tonometer, ophthalmoscope) plus UI icons: coin, gem, star, trophy, flame, clock, heart, lock, unlock, chevron-left/right, close, check, x, settings, sound-on, sound-off, gift, crate, eye, chart, user, users, crown, lightning, sparkle, book, play, pause, refresh, info, warning, alert. Export the icon name union type.

4) Hooks: useSfx() that returns a play(id) function using services.audio when inside a ServicesProvider and a no-op otherwise; useReducedMotion(); useInterval/useAnimationFrame helpers that clean up.

5) Sandbox page src/app/sandbox/pages/ui-kit.tsx (default export { id: 'ui-kit', title, component }) showcasing every component and the icon grid on top of the Backdrop — this is how reviewers judge you; make it look like a premium design-system showcase. View it at ?sandbox=page/ui-kit. Keep each component in its own file under src/ui-kit/components/. Export everything from src/ui-kit/index.ts.

Implement createAudio(): AudioPort in src/audio (keep that export name/signature) — a fully PROCEDURAL WebAudio engine (no audio files). Requirements:
- Every SfxId in src/core/ports.ts gets a distinct, premium, cohesive sound designed with oscillators, FM, filtered noise, envelopes, convolution/feedback-delay shimmer: think glass chimes, brass instruments, soft clicks, warm coins, magical sparkles. 'lens-click' and 'dial' should feel like precise optical hardware; 'coin(s)' satisfying; 'levelup'/'legendary'/'rare' escalating fanfares; 'fail'/'error' gentle but clear (never harsh); 'heartbeat' and 'alarm' for emergencies; 'countdown'/'tick' for timers; 'stamp' for the grade stamp; 'door' for a patient entering; 'streak-fire' whooshy; 'chest-open' anticipatory. Musical: tune pitched sounds to one key (e.g. D major / D lydian) so they harmonise with music.
- play(id, {volume, pitch}) with small random pitch/volume variation to avoid fatigue, voice limiting (max simultaneous instances per id), and a tiny cooldown for spammy ids like 'hover'.
- music(track | null): generative, endlessly varying ambient music per TrackId — title (wondrous: lush detuned pads, celesta/glass arpeggios, slow evolving chords), hub (warm lo-fi clinic: soft keys, gentle pulse), exam (focused, minimal, light pulse), emergency (tense: low drone, heartbeat kick, rising filter), results (triumphant shimmer), zen (soft, sparse). Smooth 1.5-2s crossfades between tracks; schedule with the AudioContext clock (lookahead scheduler), not setInterval jitter. Keep CPU low.
- setVolumes({master,sfx,music}) with smooth gain ramps; unlock() resumes the context on the first user gesture; music requested before unlock starts once unlocked.
- Must be completely safe where AudioContext is missing (happy-dom tests, old browsers): degrade to no-ops, never throw. Pause music when document is hidden.
- Structure: engine/context management, sfx library (one small file per family is fine), music engine (instruments + sequencer + per-track compositions), a mixer. Unit-test the pure parts (scales, note math, scheduler logic, voice limiting) with vitest.
- Sandbox page src/app/sandbox/pages/audio.tsx (default export { id: 'audio', title, component: (p:{services}) => ... }) — a beautiful little mixing-desk page: buttons to audition every SFX and every music track, volume sliders. Note: the sandbox passes `services` whose audio is the real createAudio() instance, so drive it via props.services.audio. Reviewers cannot hear audio; they will judge the code (sound design quality, scheduling correctness) and the page visuals.

Two shared rendering libraries (src/render/index.ts already re-exports ./fx and ./avatar — keep the createFx signature exactly).

A) FX — createFx(layer: HTMLElement, shakeTarget: HTMLElement, opts: { reducedMotion: () => boolean }): FxPort (contract in src/core/ports.ts). A full-screen canvas inside `layer` (DPR-aware, resizes, RAF only while particles are alive). Pooled particle system with gravity/drag/rotation/fade; kinds: confetti (tumbling ribbons in palette colours), sparks (additive glowing streaks), coins (spinning gold coins with highlight that arc and fall), stars (twinkling 4-point stars), hearts, embers (rising glowing motes). burst(x,y,{kind,count,color}). floatText: DOM element rising + fading with Space Grotesk numbers and glow. shake(strength, ms): decaying perlin/noise translate+rotate on shakeTarget (restore transform exactly). flash(color, ms) full-screen additive flash. vignette(color, ms) pulsing edge glow. hitstop(ms): freeze particle sim and add a brief CSS class 'fx-hitstop' on shakeTarget (e.g. tiny scale punch). Reduced motion: no shake, no flash, 30% particles. Clean, framework-free TS.

B) AVATAR — gorgeous procedural patient portraits. Export a Preact component <PatientAvatar spec={AvatarSpec} age sex expression? external? lookAt? size? animated? /> and a pure function generateAvatar(rng: Rng, opts: { age: number; sex: 'F'|'M'|'X' }): AvatarSpec. Style: premium editorial vector illustration (think high-end flat illustration with soft gradient shading, rim light from a gold key light, subtle texture) — head, neck, shoulders/outfit, hair styles (all HairStyle values), facial hair, headwear, glasses styles, accessories, skin tones 0-5 (diverse, respectful), age cues (laugh lines, wrinkles, grey/white hair, age spots at 70+; children look young). Eyes are expressive with the spec's iris colour, pupils, eyelids that BLINK, gaze that follows lookAt (x,y in -1..1). Expressions: 'neutral' | 'worried' | 'pain' | 'happy' | 'relieved' | 'squint' | 'surprised' (eyebrows, mouth, eyelids). Idle animation: breathing (shoulders), micro head sway, randomised blinks (respect reduced motion via prop). Clinical visible signs from external (PatientFindings['external']): redEye per eye (injected sclera), tearing (glistening tear streak), ptosis (droopy lid on that side), proptosis, squinting, eyePatch, photophobia (shielding hand or squint), forehead dermatomal rash (shingles), plus optional strabismus prop { eye: 'OD'|'OS', direction: 'in'|'out'|'up'|'down' } to turn one eye. Remember OD = patient's RIGHT eye = viewer's LEFT. SVG output, scalable, crisp. Also export a small <AvatarBust/> variant for list rows/leaderboards (just head, circular crop, ring colour).

Sandbox pages: render-fx.tsx (buttons triggering every FX on a backdrop; click anywhere bursts) and render-avatar.tsx (a grid of ~16 generated patients of all ages/tones + a detailed panel with toggles for each expression and clinical sign). Each default export { id, title, component }. Unit-test generateAvatar determinism & validity.

Two shared, clinically faithful canvas renderers used by many mini-games (slit lamp, pupils, cover test, tonometry, fluorescein, ophthalmoscopy, retinoscopy) and by the iris collection gallery. src/render/index.ts already re-exports ./eye and ./fundus.

A) EYE CLOSE-UP — export `type EyeState`, `drawEye(ctx: CanvasRenderingContext2D, w: number, h: number, s: EyeState, t?: number)`, `eyeStateFromFindings(f: PatientFindings, eye: Eye, opts?): EyeState`, and a Preact `<EyeCanvas state={EyeState} width height />` (DPR aware, optional RAF animation for micro-saccades/tear film shimmer). EyeState covers: eye ('OD'|'OS' for nasal/temporal orientation), irisColor, irisSeed, pupilMm (scaled realistically to an ~11.5mm cornea), gaze {x,y}, lidAperture 0..1 (blink/ptosis), lighting 'room'|'penlight'|'slit'|'cobalt'|'dim', redness 0..1 with pattern 'diffuse'|'ciliary-flush'|'sectoral', subconjunctival hemorrhage, chemosis, pinguecula/pterygium (nasal), corneal edema/haze, dendrite, ulcer/infiltrate (white opacity), keratic precipitates, abrasion, foreign body, hypopyon, hyphema, AC depth (affects a van Herick slit view), lens opacity 0..1 with type nuclear(yellow-brown)/cortical(spokes)/PSC, fluorescein stain pattern (all StainPattern values: rendered bright green ONLY under cobalt light), corneal light reflex (Hirschberg) position. Iris must be STUNNING and anatomical: radial fibres, collarette, crypts, pupillary ruff, limbal ring, subtle heterochromia flecks, wet specular highlights and window reflections; plus a dark-iris variant. Also export `paintIrisArt(ctx, size, seed: number, opts: { palette: string[]; rarity: 'common'|'rare'|'epic'|'legendary' })` that paints a jewel-like, collectible iris card artwork (rarer = more exotic palettes, iridescent shimmer, stars in the pupil, etc.) for the Gallery system.
Slit-lamp support: `drawSlitSection(ctx, w, h, s: EyeState, beam: { x: number; width: number; angleDeg: number; height?: number })` rendering the optical section (corneal parallelepiped, AC gap per van Herick grade, anterior chamber cells as tiny drifting specks and flare as a hazy beam per SUN grade, lens section).

B) FUNDUS — export `paintFundus(ctx, w, h, post: PosteriorSegment, opts: { eye: Eye; seed: number; redFree?: boolean; view?: { cx: number; cy: number; zoom: number } }): FundusMap` where FundusMap gives NORMALISED (0..1) positions/radii of disc, cup, macula/fovea and every rendered lesion { type, zone, x, y, r } for hit-testing by an ophthalmoscopy spot-the-finding mini-game. Must look like a real fundus photograph: orange-red choroidal glow with radial falloff and vignette, fundusTone (light/medium/dark/tigroid choroidal vessels), correct anatomy for OD vs OS (disc nasal to fovea — OD disc on the viewer's right? CHECK: in a fundus photo of the RIGHT eye the disc appears on the RIGHT side of the image; left eye on the left), disc ~1.5mm with neuroretinal rim + cup sized by CDR, rim thinning per ISNT violations, pallor, blurred/elevated margins and disc edema (obscured vessels at margin), disc hemorrhage, procedural vascular arcades branching from the disc (arteries thinner and lighter red with central light reflex; veins darker/wider; AV ratio; AV nicking at crossings; copper wiring; tortuosity; venous dilation), macula darker with foveal light reflex. Every LesionType in core/clinical.ts rendered convincingly in its zone with density: dot-blot & flame hemorrhages, microaneurysms, cotton-wool spots, hard exudates (incl. circinate/macular star), drusen small/large, geographic atrophy, subretinal hemorrhage, neovascularization (fine frond vessels at disc/elsewhere), retinal tear (horseshoe), lattice, nevus, pigment clumping, laser scars, Hollenhorst plaque, retinal whitening, cherry-red spot, macular edema (sheen), ERM (wrinkle), macular hole, venous beading. Retinal detachment: grey-white elevated undulating retina with folds in the specified zones, macula-on/off. Vitreous haze/hemorrhage/Weiss ring as an overlay option. Deterministic per seed. Also a Preact `<FundusView post eye seed lensView? />` with drag-to-pan/zoom and an optional ophthalmoscope 'light circle' mask (dark outside a movable circle) used by ophthalmoscopy.

Sandbox pages render-eye.tsx and render-fundus.tsx (default export { id, title, component }): galleries of presets (normal, cataract, acute angle closure, uveitis, conjunctivitis, abrasion under cobalt, dendrite, pterygium; fundus: normal OD/OS, glaucoma CDR 0.8 inferior thinning, NPDR, PDR, hypertensive, dry & wet AMD, CRAO, CRVO, RD macula-off, papilledema, tigroid myope) plus a control panel. Accuracy matters: a practising optometrist will judge these images. Unit-test FundusMap geometry (disc side per eye, CDR) and determinism.

A) LEARNING (src/learning, keep exports createLearning(save, now): LearningPort and attachLearning(services): () => void). Implement an SM-2-style spaced repetition scheduler per DiagnosisId persisted in save slot 'learning' (ease factor, interval, repetitions, due timestamp, lapses, last quality, seen count). record(id, quality 0..5), due(limit) (most overdue first), mastery(id) 0..1 (blend of repetitions, ease, recency; 1 only after several spaced successes), stats() {seen, mastered (mastery>=0.8), due}. attachLearning subscribes to 'case:completed' and records the correct diagnosis with learningQuality(score) (from @core), and when the player picked a WRONG diagnosis also records a small lapse against the diagnosis they confused it with (so confusions resurface); emits 'learning:reviewed'. Thorough vitest tests with an injected clock.

B) MODES (src/modes/<id>/index.ts, each default-exports a ModeModule; one folder each; they must not import each other — shared logic comes from @core: pickCase, dayKey, createRng). Implement: 'shift' (Clinic Shift: 5 patients, difficulty window ramps with experience — track completed-case count in a save slot 'mode:shift' or use services.learning.stats(); first ever shift should start gentle, difficulty 1-2), 'rush' (Rush Hour: endless, lives 3, scoreMultiplier ~1.0 plus combo handled by RunSnapshot.combo — document how combo should multiply; mixed difficulties, prefers quick cases), 'code-red' (Code Red: only cases with emergency set OR urgency 'emergency'/'urgent'; length 4; timeLimitSec override only when a case lacks its own; locked until the player has completed at least 3 cases — read your own slot or learning stats; give a friendly locked reason), 'daily' (Daily Rounds: 3 cases chosen deterministically from createRng(dayKey(services.clock.now())); same for everyone; pickNext must return them in order), 'review' (Second Opinion: prefers cases whose diagnosis is in services.learning.due(); length 4; if nothing due, choose least-mastered diagnoses; locked reason if the player has seen < 2 diagnoses). Each mode: id, player-facing title & tagline (NO sin language — see GAME_DESIGN.md), icon (emoji is fine), accent colour from the design tokens palette, order, rules, optional internal `drive` metadata. pickNext must never return a case already in run.completed/run.failed while unseen cases remain, and must return null when the pool is empty. Unit-test every mode with a fake services built via createServices() from @core and a handful of synthetic cases.

C) Sandbox page src/app/sandbox/pages/modes.tsx (default export { id, title, component }) — a clean diagnostics page that lists registered modes, their lock state, and simulates a run (shows which case ids each mode would pick) using the registered cases, plus a learning-state table. Content (cases) may not exist yet when you build — handle empty registries gracefully.
